title: CHAPTER SIX. On the end of this world; heavens pass by free omnipotence, not natural cause
pass_a_gloss: the elements burning with heat will stand as dissolved, and the earth and the works that stand as in it will stand as burned up. From the state belonging toward the separated soul there follows the end belonging toward this world, by which the heavens (Enchiridion chapter 91) will pass away with a great noise not from a natural cause but from the free determination and omnipotence belonging toward their Creator; On the end belonging toward this world. CHAPTER SIX.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER SIX. On the end of this world.

From the state of the separated soul there follows the end of this world, by which the heavens (Enchiridion chapter 91) will pass away with a great noise not from a natural cause but from the free determination and omnipotence of their Creator; the elements burning with heat will be dissolved, and the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up.
source_text: CAPUT SEXTUM, De hujus mundi fine. A statu animae separatae sequitur hujus mundi finis, quo caeli (Enchir. c. 91.) non a causa naturali, sed ex determinatione libera & omnipotentia creatoris sui cum stridore praeteribunt; elementa aestuantia solventur, terraque & quae in ea sunt opera exurentur.
